title: t2100: chore(pulse): parent
body:
**Task ID:** `t2100` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-04-15
**Tags:** `parent` `interactive`

## Description

chore(pulse): parent — harden ratchet-down pipeline + pre-dispatch no-op validator — tracker for the #19024 post-mortem. Three children: t2101 widens dedup window, t2102 adds fresh-pull before ratchet-check, t2103 adds a pre-dispatch validator mechanism (defense in depth). Parent-task blocks dispatch unconditionally; implementation happens on children.

## Task Brief

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->
# t2100: Harden ratchet-down pipeline and add pre-dispatch no-op validator (parent)

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-04-15
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** marcusquinn (ai-interactive)
- **Parent task:** none — this IS the parent
- **Conversation context:** Triage of #19024 revealed that the pulse's ratchet-down issue generator filed a duplicate 2 minutes after the identical change (NESTING_DEPTH_THRESHOLD 284→279) had already landed in PR #19017, and the dispatched sonnet worker silently exited without closing the issue despite the "Worker triage responsibility" prompt rule. User asked for a systemic fix.

## What

Three-phase hardening of the ratchet-down pipeline plus a generalisable defense-in-depth layer:

1. **t2101 (#19036)** — Widen the dedup search window in `pulse-simplification.sh:1694-1698` to match PRs merged within the last 24h, not just open PRs. This closes the immediate duplicate-filing race.
2. **t2102 (#19037)** — Pull `$aidevops_path` fresh before running `complexity-scan-helper.sh ratchet-check` so the proposal reflects current main. Secondary cause of the #19024 duplicate.
3. **t2103 (#19038)** — New `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh` mechanism that runs an issue's own verification in a fresh checkout before the pulse spawns a worker. If the premise has been falsified (thresholds already tight, stale at dispatch time), close the issue with a rationale comment instead of burning a dispatch cycle. First concrete validator: ratchet-down.

## Why

The `#19024` incident cost a worker dispatch, a re-triage by a human, and the #19024 worker's silent exit left the issue stuck in `status:queued` — the pulse would have re-dispatched it indefinitely. Two failures compound: (a) generator filed a stale proposal, (b) worker ignored the triage prompt. Fix 1+2 eliminate the generator bug; Fix 3 is the deterministic safety net that doesn't rely on models following prompts.

## Parent task

This issue has the `parent-task` label and is `#parent` tagged. It blocks dispatch unconditionally and exists only as a tracker. Implementation happens on the three children.

## Reference

- Incident: #19024 (closed as premise falsified)
- Prior related fix: t2089 / PR #18959 (this is its symmetric completion)
- Full detail: issue body of #19035 has the complete root-cause analysis, strategy, and acceptance criteria
- Triage evidence: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/19024#issuecomment-4248172074

## Acceptance

- Children #19036, #19037, #19038 all merged
- No regression in t2089 keyword-search dedup
- Documentation for the new pre-dispatch validator mechanism
- Smoke test confirms duplicate ratchet-down issues can no longer be filed under the stale-read race

title: t2117: feat(pulse): dispatch throttle on overlapping file footprints — prevent CONFLICTING cascades at source
body:
Follow-up from t2116/GH#19106 systemic fix for worker PR loss via CONFLICTING-close. After landing the update-branch attempt and needs-maintainer-review skip, two remaining loss vectors remain.

## Problem

Multiple workers are dispatched in parallel against the same file (e.g. .agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf ratchet PRs, .agents/workflows/brief/templates.md simplification PRs). Whichever PR merges first invalidates all others. The update-branch salvage path (t2116) now rescues many of these, but some are genuine line-conflicting edits on the same hunk and still cascade through CONFLICTING-close.

## Proposed approach

Introduce a lightweight file-footprint lock in the dispatch path:
- When a brief is parsed, extract its 'Files to modify' section into a canonical file list.
- Before dispatching a new worker for an issue, check the dispatch-dedup ledger for any currently in-flight issue whose file list overlaps. If found, defer dispatch one cycle rather than parallelising.
- Decays after the blocking issue reaches status:in-review or its PR merges.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Two issues with overlapping file footprints never have simultaneous dispatched workers.
2. Issues with disjoint file footprints still dispatch in parallel (no over-serialisation).
3. Regression test in .agents/scripts/tests/ that builds a mock dispatch state and asserts the deferral.
4. Log line with (t2xxx) audit tag on every deferral.

## Context

Root-cause data and prior fix: GH#19106 / PR #19107. Relevant files:
- .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh (the dedup ledger)
- .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh (dispatch caller)
- .agents/templates/brief-template.md (Files to modify section format)

title: t2118: feat(pulse-merge): carry forward closed PR diff as worker guidance on linked issue
body:
Follow-up from t2116/GH#19106. When _close_conflicting_pr does have to close a PR for a true semantic conflict, the worker's solved diff is silently discarded and the re-dispatched worker starts from scratch — token waste, and re-produces the same race.

## Problem

Currently, a conflicting-close leaves the linked issue in its original form. The next worker reads the same brief and produces the same diff, hits the same conflict, and the loop repeats.

## Proposed approach

Before closing a CONFLICTING PR, extract its diff via gh pr diff, wrap it in a fenced block, and append it to the linked issue body under a '## Prior worker attempt (PR #NNN, closed CONFLICTING)' section. Idempotent — never append twice for the same PR. The re-dispatched worker reads the diff as work-in-progress and can rebase/apply it instead of re-deriving it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Closed CONFLICTING PR diffs appear on the linked issue body in a clearly marked section.
2. Idempotent — running the close path twice for the same PR does not duplicate the section.
3. Size-capped — diffs over 20KB are truncated with a '... (truncated, full diff at PR #NNN)' marker, so the issue body does not blow up.
4. Does not fire for origin:interactive or needs-maintainer-review skips (those paths never close now, post-t2116).
5. Regression test mirroring test-pulse-merge-update-branch.sh pattern.

## Context

Root-cause data and prior fix: GH#19106 / PR #19107. Relevant files:
- .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh (_close_conflicting_pr)

body:
## Agent doc simplification (automated scan)

**File:** `.agents/reference/pre-dispatch-validators.md`
**Detected topic:** Pre-Dispatch Validators
**Current size:** 136 lines

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

### For instruction docs — proposed action

Tighten and restructure this agent doc. Follow `tools/build-agent/build-agent.md` guidance. Key principles:

1. **Preserve all institutional knowledge** — every verbose rule exists because something broke without it. Do not remove task IDs, incident references, error statistics, or decision rationale. Compress prose, not knowledge.
2. **Order by importance** — most critical instructions first (primacy effect: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily). Security rules, core workflow, then edge cases.
3. **Split if needed** — if the file covers multiple distinct concerns, extract sub-docs with a parent index. Use progressive disclosure (pointers, not inline content).
4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers
3. **Zero content loss** — every line moves to a chapter file, nothing is deleted or compressed
4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

### Verification

- Content preservation: all code blocks, URLs, task ID references (`tNNN`, `GH#NNN`), and command examples must be present before and after
- No broken internal links or references
- Agent behaviour unchanged (test with a representative query if possible)
- Qlty smells resolved for the target file: `~/.qlty/bin/qlty smells --all 2>&1 | grep '.agents/reference/pre-dispatch-validators.md' | grep -c . | grep -q '^0$'` (report `SKIP` if Qlty is unavailable, not `FAIL`)
- For reference corpora: `wc -l` total of chapter files >= original line count minus index overhead

### Confidence: medium

Automated scan flagged this file for maintainer review. The best simplification strategy requires human judgment — some files are appropriately structured already. Reference corpora (SKILL.md, domain knowledge bases) need restructuring into chapters, not content reduction.

- `approved` — removes the review gate and queues for automated dispatch
- `declined: <reason>` — closes this issue (include your reason after the colon)

title: t2121: fix(opencode-aidevops): buffer stream chunks by newline in stripMcpPrefix to fix tool-name truncation
body:
provider-auth-request.mjs transformResponseStream applies a regex to strip mcp__aidevops__ tool-name prefix from EACH decoded stream chunk independently. When Anthropic's SSE stream splits a tool name across two chunks (common, depends on TCP framing), the regex on either chunk fails to match — the reassembled stream has the unstripped name, OpenCode sees an unknown tool, and the model's tool call is rejected as unavailable. This is the likely cause of the intermittent 30s no_activity worker failures. Fix: buffer chunks by last newline so the regex only runs against complete SSE lines (which always contain complete JSON events).

title: discussion: review feedback gap when bot reviews fail or are rate-limited during fast merge cycles
body:
## Description

When the pulse merges PRs faster than review bots can complete analysis, a compounding feedback gap emerges: CodeRabbit posts "Review failed — closed" or "Rate limit exceeded", Gemini hits daily quota, and the existing sweep mechanisms have nothing to extract because no review ever completed. The code reaches main with zero bot review and no recovery path.

This isn't a bug report — the current behavior matches the design intent in GH#17549 ("Pass immediately... Waiting gains nothing"). This is a discussion about whether the feedback gap warrants a detection or recovery mechanism, and what the intended design posture is.

## Observed Behavior

On a private repo (12 PRs via pulse/supervisor dispatch, 06:19-06:47 UTC):

| Outcome | Count | Details |
|---------|-------|---------|
| "Review failed — closed" | 6 | CodeRabbit started analysis, PR merged before it could post |
| "Rate limit exceeded" | 5 | CodeRabbit hourly commit limit hit |
| Actual CodeRabbit review | 1 | PR waited 50 min before merge |
| Gemini reviews | 0 of 12 | Daily quota exhausted |

Result: 11 of 12 PRs merged with zero bot review. The post-merge-review-scanner ran afterward and correctly created 0 followup issues — there were no review findings to extract. The same pattern (7-22s merge times, rate-limited CodeRabbit) was observed on the aidevops repo itself (PRs #19143-19170).

## How the gap compounds

1. **Failed reviews consume quota**: When a PR merges before CodeRabbit finishes, CodeRabbit still generates a walkthrough summary and posts "Review failed — closed." This likely counts against the hourly commit limit, burning quota on reviews that produce no findings and triggering rate limits on subsequent PRs.

2. **Rate-limited PRs pass the gate immediately**: `PASS_RATE_LIMITED` in `review-bot-gate-helper.sh` returns exit 0 with no wait (GH#17549). The code comment says "The bot will review post-merge when its rate limit resets" — but CodeRabbit does not review merged/closed PRs. It posts "Review failed — The pull request is closed" and stops.

3. **No sweep detects the absence of review**: The post-merge-review-scanner and quality-feedback scan-merged extract *findings from reviews that happened*. The daily quality sweep runs repo-wide tools (ShellCheck, Qlty, CodeRabbit codebase review). None of these check whether a specific PR was reviewed — they only process findings when reviews exist. This is reasonable for clean PRs (reviewed, no issues), but means "never reviewed" and "reviewed, no issues" are indistinguishable.

4. **`batch-retry` only reaches open PRs**: Uses `gh pr list --state open`. By the time rate limits reset, PRs are merged and invisible to this mechanism.

5. **Gemini provides partial coverage on lower-volume cycles**: On normal days, Gemini posts formal reviews (even after merge) that the scanner picks up. The gap manifests when both bots are exhausted simultaneously.

## Questions for discussion

1. **Is the `PASS_RATE_LIMITED` comment accurate?** GH#17549 says "The bot will review post-merge when its rate limit resets." From observation, CodeRabbit does not come back to review merged PRs. If that assumption informed the "pass immediately" design, the premise may be worth revisiting.

2. **Would a "zero-review detector" add value?** A lightweight post-merge check that flags PRs with 0 formal reviews and 0 inline comments from any known bot. Not to create findings (there are none), but to surface the coverage gap — e.g., as a metric in the supervisor issue, or as a signal to throttle dispatch rate for that repo.

3. **Would dispatch-rate awareness help?** If the pulse tracked CodeRabbit's hourly limit (or detected rate-limit comments on recent PRs) and staggered worker dispatch accordingly, it could prevent the exhaustion cascade. Trade-off is slower throughput vs guaranteed review coverage.

## Related Issues

- GH#17541: workers self-merge without review-bot-gate (fixed — worker merge path gated)
- GH#2980: gate returns PASS on rate-limit notices (fixed — pattern detection added)
- GH#3827: CodeRabbit rate-limited on 14+ PRs (fixed — grace period added)

These addressed gate behavior. This discussion is about the end-to-end feedback loop after those fixes.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.8.41
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0

title: t2122: fix(opencode-plugin): extend Response.json() fix to remaining Bun.serve callers
body:
**Task ID:** `t2122` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~45m`
**Logged:** 2026-04-15
**Tags:** `bug` `opencode` `interactive`

## Description

fix(opencode-plugin): extend Response.json() fix to remaining Bun.serve callers — follow-up to PR #19174 (superdav42 claude+google proxy fix). The `_Response` type-mismatch bug exists in 3 untouched plugin files with `Bun.serve`-backed fetch handlers: `cursor/proxy.js` (5 JSON call sites + 1 404, owns its own `Bun.serve` at line 160), `cursor/proxy-stream.js` (1 SSE streaming response), and `provider-auth-request.mjs` (1 streaming passthrough). Extracts `jsonResponse`/`textResponse` into a new shared `response-helpers.mjs` module (single audited call site for the realm-boundary workaround) and routes all 7 sites through it. Does NOT touch `claude-proxy.mjs` or `google-proxy.mjs` — those files carry the duplicated helper from #19174 and will be consolidated in a follow-up after #19174 merges to avoid a trivial conflict. Adds `tests/test-opencode-response-helpers.sh` with syntax-check + 5 runtime assertions.

## Task Brief

# t2122: Extend Response.json() fix to remaining opencode plugin Bun.serve callers

**Session origin:** interactive (follow-up filed during `/review-issue-pr 19174` with marcusquinn)

**Ref:** GH#19175 | **Parent:** PR #19174 (superdav42, claude+google proxy fix)

## What

Stop the `Expected a Response object, but received '_Response'` error from
recurring in the three opencode plugin files that PR #19174 does not touch.
Introduce a shared `response-helpers.mjs` module so the fix lives in exactly
one place for the whole plugin, and route the untouched call sites through
it.

Files changed:

- NEW: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/response-helpers.mjs` — shared
  `jsonResponse(data, init?)` and `textResponse(body, init?)` helpers with a
  cross-realm-safe path (`Response.json()` when available) and a
  documented fallback. Source of truth for the workaround.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/cursor/proxy.js` — 5 `new Response(...)`
  call sites migrated (4 `jsonResponse`, 1 `textResponse` 404). Adds one
  import line.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/cursor/proxy-stream.js` — 1 SSE
  streaming response routed through `textResponse` for consistency.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth-request.mjs` — 1
  streaming passthrough routed through `textResponse`.
- NEW: `tests/test-opencode-response-helpers.sh` — smoke test (syntax-check
  + runtime behaviour assertions for `jsonResponse`/`textResponse`).

**Out of scope (deferred to a follow-up after #19174 merges):**

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/claude-proxy.mjs` and `google-proxy.mjs`
  currently duplicate `jsonResponse`/`textResponse` locally (as introduced
  by #19174). They should eventually import from `response-helpers.mjs`
  instead, but that migration has to wait until #19174 merges to avoid a
  trivial merge conflict. A follow-up PR will delete the two local copies
  and add the import. This PR deliberately does not touch those files.

## Why

PR #19174 (landing the `Response.json()` fix for claude-proxy and
google-proxy) is a strict net improvement with 42 minutes of clean journal
evidence, but the same idiom exists in four other files in the same plugin:
`cursor/proxy.js` (with its own `Bun.serve` at line 160), `cursor/proxy-stream.js`,
and `provider-auth-request.mjs`. If the author's root-cause hypothesis
(plugin loader rebinds `Response` to a realm-local `_Response`) is correct,
these are dormant time-bombs — any user who enables the Cursor provider
will hit the exact same journal spam as soon as the proxy handles a
`/v1/models` request or a non-streaming completion.

Rather than ship another round of "fix it where the user reported it", this
task:

1. Factors the helper out of the two files that `#19174` duplicates it into,
   so the plugin has a single audited call site for the workaround.
2. Applies the helper to the three new files. The JSON call sites in
   `cursor/proxy.js` are the real fix; the `textResponse` migrations on the
   streaming paths are consistency-only (streaming has never been observed
   to trip the mismatch in practice, per `#19174`'s own evidence), but
   funnel all response construction through the same module so a future
   workaround lands in one place.

## How

1. **Memory + discovery pass done** — `git log` on the plugin shows no
   in-flight work on these files (#19164 was a stream-chunking fix in a
   different file; #18906 was the decomposition that created `cursor/proxy.js`
   as a standalone). Memory had no prior entries for this class of bug.

2. **Create `response-helpers.mjs`** with `jsonResponse` using `Response.json`
   when available and a `new Response(JSON.stringify(...))` fallback
   matching the Content-Type header pattern from #19174. `textResponse` is
   a thin alias over `new Response(...)` kept for consistency — the module
   docstring documents the empirical observation that streaming paths have
   not been affected and the alias exists to centralise the fix if that
   ever changes.

3. **Migrate cursor/proxy.js** — add one import line, replace 5 call sites.
   Model the call-site shape on #19174's transformations in `claude-proxy.mjs`
   (e.g., error payloads collapse `{status, headers: {Content-Type: ...}}`
   to `{status}` since `jsonResponse` sets the header itself).

4. **Migrate cursor/proxy-stream.js** and **provider-auth-request.mjs** —
   add one import each, replace 1 call site each with `textResponse`.
   These streaming paths have not been observed to fail, but consistency
   is cheap and the alias is free.

5. **Test** — `tests/test-opencode-response-helpers.sh` runs `node --check`
   on all four files plus a runtime assertion that `jsonResponse` and
   `textResponse` return valid `Response` objects, round-trip JSON and text
   bodies, honour custom status codes, and accept `ReadableStream` bodies.
   Shellcheck clean. Real acceptance is the OpenCode journal — see below.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `response-helpers.mjs` exists and exports `jsonResponse`, `textResponse`
- [x] `cursor/proxy.js` has zero `new Response(...)` call sites; all 5 routed through helpers
- [x] `cursor/proxy-stream.js` SSE response routed through `textResponse`
- [x] `provider-auth-request.mjs` streaming passthrough routed through `textResponse`
- [x] `node --check` clean on all four modified files
- [x] `tests/test-opencode-response-helpers.sh` passes (5 assertions)
- [x] `shellcheck` clean on the new test script
- [ ] **Runtime verification (pending user):** after merge, restart
      `opencode-web.service` and tail the journal for 30+ minutes without
      seeing `Expected a Response object, but received '_Response'`.
      Parallel to #19174's existing 42-min clean run.
- [x] Does NOT touch `claude-proxy.mjs` or `google-proxy.mjs` (follow-up
      consolidation deferred until #19174 merges)

## Context

- **Parent PR:** #19174 — original `Response.json()` fix for claude+google.
  42-min clean runtime, mergeable, approve gate satisfied.
- **Root cause (not fixable here):** OpenCode's Bun plugin loader runs
  plugin code in a context where `globalThis.Response` may resolve to a
  different class identity than the one `Bun.serve`'s native fetch
  dispatcher type-checks against. This is an upstream OpenCode/Bun
  interaction; our fix is a stable symptom workaround.
- **Why `Response.json()` works:** static Fetch API method implemented
  natively in Bun, bypasses the user-visible constructor and returns an
  instance blessed by Bun's internal path.
- **Why the streaming `textResponse` migration is consistency-only:**
  PR #19174's own helper uses raw `new Response()` for streaming bodies
  and has a 42-min clean run, suggesting the bug is specific to the
  JSON-stringify + Content-Type init shape, not streaming. The alias
  gives us a single call site to patch if we ever see otherwise.
- **Tier:** `tier:simple` — verbatim oldString/newString replacements in
  4 files, one new file under 100 lines, clear acceptance criteria,
  single-estimate under 1h.

title: t2123: Configurable review gate rate-limit behavior per tool and per repo
body:
## What

Make the `PASS_RATE_LIMITED` behavior in `review-bot-gate-helper.sh` configurable at three levels:

1. **Global default** — `REVIEW_GATE_RATE_LIMIT_BEHAVIOR` env var or entry in a framework config file. Default: `pass` (current behavior).
2. **Per-repo in `repos.json`** — a `review_gate` object on each repo entry with a default and per-tool overrides.
3. **Per-tool granularity** — different auditing tools (CodeRabbit, Gemini, Qlty, Copilot, etc.) have different rate limits and value. Users should control behavior per tool.

## Why

GH#19173 identified a real feedback gap: when bots are rate-limited, PRs merge with zero review and the code comment claiming "the bot will review post-merge" is incorrect. The daily sweep provides codebase-level coverage, but users who pay for higher rate limits or want stricter per-PR review coverage should be able to opt in to waiting.

The current `pass` default is correct for maintainer/worker PRs. This makes it configurable, not changing the default.

## How

### Schema design for `repos.json`

```json
{
  "path": "/Users/example/Git/myrepo",
  "slug": "owner/myrepo",
  "pulse": true,
  "review_gate": {
    "rate_limit_behavior": "pass",
    "tools": {
      "coderabbitai": { "rate_limit_behavior": "wait" },
      "gemini-code-assist": { "rate_limit_behavior": "pass" }
    }
  }
}
```

Resolution order: per-tool setting > per-repo `review_gate.rate_limit_behavior` > global env `REVIEW_GATE_RATE_LIMIT_BEHAVIOR` > hardcoded `pass`.

Values: `pass` (current — exit 0 immediately), `wait` (return exit 1, let the gate retry loop handle it).

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh:326-334` — replace hardcoded `PASS_RATE_LIMITED` with config lookup. The rate-limited bot names are already in `$rate_limited_bots`; iterate and check per-tool config.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh:328-329` — fix inaccurate code comment claiming bots review post-merge.
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — document the `review_gate` repos.json field alongside other per-repo fields.
- Reference pattern: follow the `foss_config` object pattern already in repos.json for per-repo nested config.

### Global default

Add `REVIEW_GATE_RATE_LIMIT_BEHAVIOR` to `shared-constants.sh` with default `pass`. The env var override follows the existing pattern for `PULSE_SCOPE_REPOS` and similar.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With no config changes, behavior is identical to current (pass on rate limit) — backward compatible
2. Setting `review_gate.tools.coderabbitai.rate_limit_behavior: "wait"` in a repo's repos.json entry causes the gate to return `WAITING` instead of `PASS_RATE_LIMITED` when CodeRabbit is rate-limited
3. Per-repo default (`review_gate.rate_limit_behavior`) applies to all tools not explicitly configured
4. Global env var `REVIEW_GATE_RATE_LIMIT_BEHAVIOR` applies when no per-repo config exists
5. The inaccurate code comment at line 328-329 is corrected
6. AGENTS.md documents the new `review_gate` field

## Context

- Spawned from: GH#19173 (discussion)
- Current behavior: `review-bot-gate-helper.sh:326-334`
- Known bots: `coderabbitai`, `gemini-code-assist`, `augment-code`, `augmentcode`, `copilot`
- Existing per-repo config pattern: `foss_config` in repos.json

This parent tracks the decomposition campaign that clears those 20 and builds buffer under `QLTY_SMELL_THRESHOLD`.

## What

Planning-only tracker for the file-complexity decomposition campaign. No code is committed against this issue directly — every code change lands under one of the 5 child cluster tasks. This issue is marked `parent-task` so the pulse never dispatches a worker against it.

When all 5 children merge, the aidevops repo should show:

- `qlty:file-complexity` smell count on target files: **0 of 20**
- Overall `qlty smells --all` count: **≤ 10** (20 starting minus 14+ clearable files; conservative — some residual may remain)
- `QLTY_SMELL_THRESHOLD` in `complexity-thresholds.conf`: ratcheted down from 22 to `new_count + 2` (auto-ratchet via t2067)
- Headroom for at least one new medium-complexity file landing without flipping the grade

## Why

**Zero headroom is fragile.** We are at exactly 20 smells and grade-A cutoff is ≤ 20. One new file at complexity >60 (roughly a 600-line module) flips us to B. The last 20 smells are disproportionately concentrated in 4 file families (higgsfield, oauth-pool plugin, email pipeline, doc indexing), each of which can be decomposed using patterns already proven in PR #18893 (claude-proxy), PR #18906 (opencode plugin cluster), PR #18948 (higgsfield cluster partial), and PR #19013 (the 39→20 sweep).

Shipping these 5 cluster tasks:

1. Drops total smell count from 20 to ~5 (estimated, assuming each cluster clears its listed files)
2. Gives `QLTY_SMELL_THRESHOLD` room to ratchet down, which hardens the regression gate
3. Leaves only the smallest/hardest files for a future phase-3 cleanup (none of which are near the grade threshold individually)

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking` (parent-task — never dispatched, tier is documentary only)

**Tier rationale:** Parent tasks are not dispatched by the pulse (`parent-task` label short-circuits the dispatch-dedup guard per t1986). The tier is set to `tier:thinking` only to reflect the complexity of the overall campaign for maintainers browsing the issue list.

## PR Conventions

**This is a `parent-task` — child PRs MUST use `For #19222` or `Ref #19222`, NEVER `Closes`/`Resolves`/`Fixes`.** The final cluster PR (whichever lands last) uses `Closes #19222` to close the parent. Enforced by `.github/workflows/parent-task-keyword-check.yml` and `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr`.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `NONE` — this is a planning-only tracker. All file changes happen under the child cluster tasks.

### Implementation Steps

No implementation steps. See children:

- **t2127 (#19223)** — higgsfield residual cluster (4 files)
- **t2128 (#19224)** — oauth-pool plugin cluster (3 files)
- **t2129 (#19225)** — email pipeline python cluster (5 files)

### Verification

# After ALL five children merge:
qlty smells --all --sarif 2>/dev/null | jq '.runs[0].results | length'
# Expected: ≤ 10 (upper bound; actual likely 3-6)

# QLTY_SMELL_THRESHOLD ratcheted down:
grep '^QLTY_SMELL_THRESHOLD=' .agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf
# Expected: value decreased from 22, matching new_count + 2
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All 5 child cluster issues closed via merged PR
  ```yaml

    method: bash
    run: "for n in 19223 19224 19225 19226 19227; do gh issue view $n --json state -q .state | grep -q CLOSED || exit 1; done"
  ```
- [ ] `qlty smells --all` total count is ≤ 10
  ```yaml

    method: bash
    run: "test $(qlty smells --all --sarif 2>/dev/null | jq '.runs[0].results | length') -le 10"
  ```
- [ ] Grade A maintained in `stats-quality-sweep.sh` dashboard (QLTY_GRADE_A_MAX=20, actual ≤ 20)
  ```yaml

    method: manual
    prompt: "Check daily quality sweep output — grade is A"
  ```
- [ ] `QLTY_SMELL_THRESHOLD` ratcheted down by at least 10 (from 22 to ≤ 12)
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "test $(grep '^QLTY_SMELL_THRESHOLD=' .agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf | cut -d= -f2) -le 12"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- **Cluster-per-task over file-per-task:** PRs #18893, #18906, #18948 all shipped multi-file decompositions in single PRs. Matches the natural coupling (files in `higgsfield/` share state, files in `opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool*` share the rotation layer). One-file-per-task would create 20 worker dispatches and 20 PRs for work that logically belongs in 5 units.
- **tier:thinking for clusters:** decomposition is design work, not transcription. The worker decides the module boundary — no pre-drawn line in the brief. Haiku/Sonnet routinely produce shallow splits that just move complexity around without reducing it.
- **Parent-task pattern:** `#parent` tag keeps this issue out of dispatch rotation while preserving the one-stop audit trail. See t1986 / `reference/planning-detail.md`.
- **Auto-ratchet dependency:** t2067 (auto-ratchet) is already merged. Each cluster merge automatically tightens `QLTY_SMELL_THRESHOLD`, so this campaign is self-enforcing — you cannot ship the first cluster and then silently regress.
- **Non-goal — clearing the residual Python scripts in t2131 completely.** The 3 files there (voice-bridge 95, normalise-markdown 80, tabby-profile-sync 76) are modestly over the threshold. If one proves hard to split cleanly, the worker may leave it and document why; the campaign still succeeds if 17/20 smells clear.

## Agent doc simplification (automated scan)

**File:** `.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md`
**Detected topic:** Shell Helper Style Guide
**Current size:** 143 lines

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

### For instruction docs — proposed action

Tighten and restructure this agent doc. Follow `tools/build-agent/build-agent.md` guidance. Key principles:

1. **Preserve all institutional knowledge** — every verbose rule exists because something broke without it. Do not remove task IDs, incident references, error statistics, or decision rationale. Compress prose, not knowledge.
2. **Order by importance** — most critical instructions first (primacy effect: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily). Security rules, core workflow, then edge cases.
3. **Split if needed** — if the file covers multiple distinct concerns, extract sub-docs with a parent index. Use progressive disclosure (pointers, not inline content).
4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers
3. **Zero content loss** — every line moves to a chapter file, nothing is deleted or compressed
4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

### Verification

- Content preservation: all code blocks, URLs, task ID references (`tNNN`, `GH#NNN`), and command examples must be present before and after
- No broken internal links or references
- Agent behaviour unchanged (test with a representative query if possible)
- Qlty smells resolved for the target file: `~/.qlty/bin/qlty smells --all 2>&1 | grep '.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md' | grep -c . | grep -q '^0$'` (report `SKIP` if Qlty is unavailable, not `FAIL`)
- For reference corpora: `wc -l` total of chapter files >= original line count minus index overhead

### Confidence: medium

Automated scan flagged this file for maintainer review. The best simplification strategy requires human judgment — some files are appropriately structured already. Reference corpora (SKILL.md, domain knowledge bases) need restructuring into chapters, not content reduction.

title: t2132: fix(dispatch): interactive claims broken by stale-recovery + auto-claim conflation
body:
## Summary

5 gaps in the interactive claim system cause the pulse stale-recovery to strip interactive claims after 10 minutes, and `claim-task-id.sh` to auto-claim `#auto-dispatch` tasks intended for workers.

**Observed on #19223-#19227:** interactive session created 5 `auto-dispatch` tasks. `claim-task-id.sh` auto-claimed all 5 with `status:in-review`. Alex-solovyev's pulse stripped the claims 12 minutes later via `_is_stale_assignment` (comment pattern mismatch + 600s threshold exceeded). Workers then dispatched against tasks that were still being briefed.

## Root Causes

1. **Interactive claim comment doesn't match stale-recovery sentinel** — `_is_stale_assignment` looks for `"Dispatching worker|DISPATCH_CLAIM|Worker (PID"` but interactive claims post `"Interactive session claimed"` → treated as "no dispatch comment"
2. **`_is_stale_assignment` ignores `origin:interactive`** — should short-circuit: interactive label present → NOT stale
3. **`claim-task-id.sh` auto-claims `auto-dispatch` tasks** — `_interactive_session_auto_claim_new_task` fires unconditionally in interactive sessions, even when `auto-dispatch` label signals worker intent
4. **600s stale threshold too short for interactive** — interactive sessions routinely go 30-60+ min between actions; 10 min = no protection
5. **Cross-runner stale recovery strips interactive claims** — no runner-identity check on interactive claims

## Fixes

- **A:** `_is_stale_assignment` short-circuits when `origin:interactive` present + add `"Interactive session claimed"` to sentinel patterns
- **B:** `_interactive_session_auto_claim_new_task` skips when `TASK_LABELS` contains `auto-dispatch`
- **C:** New `INTERACTIVE_STALE_THRESHOLD_SECONDS` (default 7200s) used when `origin:interactive` present
- **D:** sentinel pattern expansion (part of Fix A)

## Verification

```bash
# Test stale recovery respects interactive claims:
# Mock issue with origin:interactive + no dispatch comment + age > 600s → must NOT recover

# Test auto-claim skip:
# claim-task-id.sh --labels "auto-dispatch,tier:standard" in interactive session → must NOT apply status:in-review
```

title: t2137: fix(issue-sync): skip closing hygiene on parent-task issues + atomic status:done mutation
body:
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->

# t2137 — fix(issue-sync): skip closing hygiene on parent-task issues + atomic status:done mutation

## Session Origin

Interactive session, 2026-04-16. Surfaced while merging PR #19228 (t2126 plan
PR). Observed two systemic defects in `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` that
affect every PR merge:

1. Parent-task issue #19222 received `status:done` despite PR using the
   `For #19222` keyword (t2046 parent-task convention), because the
   workflow's title-fallback `tNNN:` search ignored the `parent-task` label.
2. `status:done` was added and `status:in-review` was removed in two separate
   `gh issue edit` calls ~5 seconds apart — violates the atomicity contract
   the framework established in t2040 (`_mark_issue_done`) for the bash helper
   path, but the workflow was never updated to match.

## What

Two surgical edits to `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` `sync-on-pr-merge`
job, plus test coverage.

### Fix 1: skip parent-task issues in title-fallback

In the `find-issue` step (around line 335-358), after a title-based
`tNNN:` search returns a candidate issue, check whether that issue carries
the `parent-task` label. If yes, drop it from `found_issues` output with a
clear log line.

**Why title-fallback only, not the Closes/Fixes/Resolves path:** explicit
Closes/Fixes/Resolves on a parent-task is either (a) the legitimate terminal
phase closing the parent, or (b) already prevented by
`parent-task-keyword-check.yml`. Respecting the keyword is correct
behaviour in both cases. The title-fallback is the gap where intent is
ambiguous — a planning PR with title `t2126:` legitimately references the
parent but isn't closing it.

### Fix 2: atomic label mutation

In the `Apply closing hygiene` step (lines 443-450), collapse the 1
`--add-label` call + 7 `--remove-label` calls (8 sequential API calls) into
a single `gh issue edit` invocation with repeated flags.

GitHub's issue edit API supports multiple `--add-label` and `--remove-label`
on one call; the resulting `labeled`/`unlabeled` events carry identical
timestamps, closing the race window entirely.

### Test coverage

Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-label-invariants.sh` (or add a sibling
test) with a case that extracts the gh invocation list from the workflow
yaml (by parsing the `Apply closing hygiene` step) and asserts exactly one
`gh issue edit` call in the status-mutation block.

## Why

- Every parent-task planning PR has silently flipped its parent to
  `status:done` since parent-task convention was introduced. Parents with
  verification work still to do are incorrectly categorised, affecting
  triage, dispatch dedup, and the status-label state machine. Observed on
  #19222 after PR #19228 merged — all 5 children coincidentally closed too,
  so the false positive wasn't caught earlier.
- The non-atomic window is narrow (5s observed) but arbitrary under API
  latency; t2040's own code comment explicitly warns *"the reconciler's
  label-invariant pass would see two status labels and could pick the wrong
  survivor, potentially losing `done`"*. The framework already acknowledges
  this as a known risk class.
- Duplicated logic between the bash helper and the workflow is the root
  cause of the divergence — t2040 fixed one copy, the other drifted.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml`
  - Lines ~335-358 (`find-issue` step): add parent-task label probe before
    writing `found_issues` output.
  - Lines ~443-450 (label mutation block): collapse to one `gh issue edit`
    call.
- **NEW or EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-label-invariants.sh` (or
  new `test-workflow-label-atomicity.sh`): assert single-edit invariant.

### Reference patterns

- **Existing skip-hygiene pattern:** lines 384-402 in the same file
  (`IS_REJECTED` path for rejection labels — `invalid`, `not-planned`,
  `wontfix`, `duplicate`). My parent-task skip follows the identical shape.
  Prior art: PR #17986 established this pattern.
- **Atomic bash helper:** `_mark_issue_done` → `set_issue_status` in
  `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh:374`. Do not call this from the
  workflow (requires sourcing the whole helper); instead inline a single
  `gh issue edit` with the equivalent flag set.

### Verification

- **Shellcheck:** `shellcheck .github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` (via
  `actionlint` if available; otherwise the embedded `run:` blocks should
  pass manual review).
- **Test:** `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-label-invariants.sh` must
  remain green; new workflow-atomicity test must assert single-edit invariant.
- **Dry-run reasoning:** trace the workflow logic against the t2126/19228
  scenario — parent-task issue #19222 with `For #19222` should produce
  `LINKED_ISSUES=""`, `FOUND_ISSUES=""` (because parent-task skip), therefore
  `ALL_ISSUES=""`, therefore early exit at line 376-378. No comment, no label
  mutation. Correct.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parent-task issue with `For #NNN`-only PR merge does NOT receive
  `status:done` label or "Completed via" comment.
- [ ] Non-parent issue with `Closes/Fixes/Resolves #NNN` PR merge still
  receives full closing hygiene (comment + atomic label edit). Baseline
  behaviour preserved.
- [ ] Label mutation is a single `gh issue edit` call — measurable by the
  timestamp of the resulting `labeled`/`unlabeled` events (<1s apart).
- [ ] `test-label-invariants.sh` (or equivalent new test) green.
- [ ] No new shellcheck findings on the workflow `run:` blocks.

## Context

- **Parent-task convention:** `prompts/build.txt` "Parent-task PR keyword
  rule (t2046)" and `templates/brief-template.md` "PR Conventions".
- **t2040 atomicity fix:** `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh:360-378`
  (commented explicitly — useful reference for the why).
- **Existing closing-hygiene skip pattern (prior art):** PR #17986.
- **Observation session:** merge of PR #19238 then PR #19228 on 2026-04-16.
  Event timeline on #19222: `status:done` added at `03:12:20Z`,
  `status:in-review` removed at `03:12:25Z` (5s gap → 8 sequential
  `gh issue edit` calls).

## Tier checklist

- [x] Single-file surgical change in one workflow + one test → would fit
  `tier:simple` except brief needs narrative trade-off reasoning
- [ ] Default `tier:standard` because bug-fix touching CI behaviour requires
  context-aware verification (won't ship if downstream workflows break)
- [x] Estimate ~45min (diff ~30 lines + test) — dispatchable as standard

## CI/CD consequence audit

The user explicitly flagged "ensuring no unintended undesirable consequences
for our CI/CD needs and aims". Changes audited against aims:

| Aim | Current | After fix | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mark issues done on merge | Works for leaf issues; over-applies to parent-tasks | Works for leaf issues; correctly skips parent-tasks | None |
| Post closing comment audit trail | Posts "Completed via…" on all linked | Still posts on leaf; skips on parent (incorrect "Completed via" message) | Audit trail on parent moves to the existing "Parent-task phase nudge" step (line 460+) which is more accurate |
| Remove stale status labels | 7 separate API calls, 5s window | Single atomic call | Downstream `issues.labeled` triggers still fire — event semantics unchanged |
| Support rejection labels (not-planned/wontfix) | Skip hygiene path at line 400 | Unchanged | None — my skip is additive |
| Support `Closes/Fixes/Resolves` → parent-task (terminal phase) | Hygiene runs (correct) | Hygiene runs (correct) | None — skip only applies to title-fallback |
| Concurrency across multiple PRs merging | `concurrency: group: issue-sync-pr-<PR>` serialises | Unchanged | None |

**Net:** strictly corrective. No new failure modes introduced, one false-positive
class eliminated, one atomicity race closed.

title: t2138: fix(pulse): reconcile_completed_parent_tasks consults sub-issue graph before body regex
body:
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->

# t2138 — fix(pulse): `reconcile_completed_parent_tasks` consults sub-issue graph before body regex

## Session Origin

Interactive session, 2026-04-16. Surfaced while inspecting parent issue
#19222 (t2126). Parent body is narrative prose with no `#NNN` references;
its 5 children (#19223-#19227) are all CLOSED and are wired via GitHub's
GraphQL `subIssues` relationship (per PR #19228's own body: "All 5 children
are wired as sub-issues of the parent via the GitHub GraphQL API"). The
reconciler (`pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:reconcile_completed_parent_tasks`,
shipped in PR #19211) relies on body regex `grep -oE '#[0-9]+'` — which
finds nothing — so the parent stays open forever.

## What

Upgrade `reconcile_completed_parent_tasks` to prefer GitHub's native
sub-issue graph. When the graph has children, use that as the authoritative
source. Fall back to body-regex only when the graph returns empty (legacy
parents that pre-date sub-issue wiring).

## Why

- **Correctness**: sub-issue graph is the canonical parent-child
  relationship on GitHub; body regex is a heuristic. When they disagree,
  the graph wins.
- **Adoption alignment**: since PR #19098 (t2114), the framework actively
  backfills sub-issue graph edges via `issue-sync-helper.sh
  backfill-sub-issues`. Most new parent-tasks use the graph. The reconciler
  must catch up.
- **Zero regression for legacy**: body-regex path is preserved as a
  fallback, so any parent that lists children only inline still closes on
  cycle.
- **Closes #19222 and any future parent in the same shape** — no
  per-parent manual body edits required.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`
  - Function `reconcile_completed_parent_tasks` (~line 964-1057).
  - Add a helper `_fetch_subissue_numbers "$slug" "$issue_num"` that runs
    one `gh api graphql` query against the `subIssues` field and emits
    newline-separated issue numbers. Returns empty string on failure, on
    missing feature, or on an empty graph.
  - In the main loop, try the graph first; if non-empty, use those numbers
    as `child_nums`. Otherwise use the existing body-regex path.
  - Preserve all existing safeguards: min 2 children, max 5 closes per
    cycle, skip unknown states, skip parents labelled with rejection
    labels.

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-reconcile-parent-task-close.sh`
  (create if absent; if present extend).
  - Mock `gh api graphql` responses for the `subIssues` query; assert
    graph-path close.
  - Mock an empty-graph response + body with `#NNN`; assert fallback-path
    close.
  - Mock a graph with one open child; assert no-close.
  - Mock a graph with <2 children; assert no-close (single-ref guard).

### Reference patterns

- **Existing GraphQL in the file**: `shared-constants.sh:1092` uses
  `gh api graphql -f query='mutation...addSubIssue...'` — the same
  invocation style applies for the `query` direction.
- **Existing reconciler structure**: `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:964-1057`
  — body-regex path stays intact as the fallback; only the "collect child
  numbers" stage gets an earlier attempt.
- **Existing test idiom**: `tests/test-label-invariants.sh` Part 3 mocks
  `gh` via `STUB_DIR/gh` and asserts on call log — same pattern applies.

### GraphQL query shape

```graphql
query($owner: String!, $name: String!, $number: Int!) {
  repository(owner: $owner, name: $name) {
    issue(number: $number) {
      subIssues(first: 50) {
        nodes { number state }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Note the `subIssues` field is GA on all GitHub tiers where AI DevOps repos
live; it returns an empty list (not an error) when the feature is unused on
an issue. Error handling:
- Non-zero exit → empty list → fall back to body regex.
- Rate limit / network → empty list → fall back (safe degrade).
- Feature-not-enabled (enterprise quirk) → empty list → fall back.

### Verification

- **Unit tests**: new `tests/test-pulse-reconcile-parent-task-close.sh` run
  under `bash` with a stubbed `gh`. Cover: graph-path close, fallback-path
  close, graph-partial-open no-close, graph-single-child no-close.
- **Static checks**: `shellcheck` on the modified helper and new test.
- **Manual integration**: on the actual #19222 after merge, watch the
  pulse log for `Reconcile parent-task: closed #19222`. If not auto-closed
  by next cycle, fall back to manual close citing the new logic (smoke
  test still validates).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `reconcile_completed_parent_tasks` queries the sub-issue graph
  before body regex.
- [ ] When graph returns ≥2 children and all are closed, the parent is
  closed with the existing summary-comment format.
- [ ] When graph returns empty, legacy body-regex path runs unchanged.
- [ ] No regression on existing safeguards (min 2 children, max 5/cycle,
  rejection-label skip, unknown-state skip).
- [ ] New test file asserts all four scenarios and passes.
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean on modified files.
- [ ] #19222 closes on the next pulse cycle post-merge (primary
  integration signal).

## Context

- **Reconciler shipped**: PR #19211 (`ff80f9523`).
- **Sub-issue infra**: PR #19098 (t2112+t2113+t2114) — `addSubIssue`
  mutation + backfill helper + CI wrapper guard.
- **Primary motivating case**: #19222 — 5 closed children via sub-issue
  graph, 0 `#NNN` references in body, reconciler can't close it.
- **GraphQL surface**: used elsewhere in `shared-constants.sh` and
  `issue-sync-helper.sh` — no new dependency.

## CI/CD consequence audit

| Aim | Current | After fix | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Close parent-tasks with all children closed | Only if body has `#NNN` | Any parent with ≥2 closed sub-issues OR ≥2 closed `#NNN` body refs | None — strictly more permissive, both signals still require ALL-closed |
| Min 2 children safeguard | Enforced | Enforced on whichever source wins | None |
| Max 5 closes per cycle | Enforced | Enforced | None |
| Rejection-label skip | Enforced (implicit via body-regex `continue`) | Explicit parity in the graph path | None |
| GraphQL rate-limits | N/A | Adds 1 query per open parent-task per cycle | Low — parent-task count is bounded (<20 typical); fall-back is safe |
| Errors on GraphQL failure | N/A | Silent fallback to body regex | None — matches existing error-tolerance pattern |
| Test coverage | None for this function | New unit test covers 4 scenarios | Improvement |

## Tier checklist

- [x] `tier:standard` — bug-fix with non-trivial logic branch, ~50 LOC

title: review-bot-gate: bot_has_real_review() false-positive on CodeRabbit placeholder comments causes merge before review completes
body:
## Description

`bot_has_real_review()` in `review-bot-gate-helper.sh` classifies CodeRabbit's initial placeholder comment as a completed review, causing PRs to merge before CodeRabbit finishes its actual review. This is a separate code path from the rate-limit handling addressed in PR #19186 — the bot is not rate-limited, it just hasn't finished yet.

CodeRabbit uses a two-phase posting pattern:
1. **Phase 1 (~14s after PR creation):** Posts an initial comment (walkthrough stub or partial content). `created_at` is set.
2. **Phase 2 (~90-120s after PR creation):** Edits the same comment with the full review (walkthrough, findings, pre-merge checks). `updated_at` is set.

The review gate sees the Phase 1 comment, checks it against `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS`, finds no match, and returns `PASS`. The worker merges after one `REVIEW_BOT_POLL_INTERVAL` cycle (~76s). CodeRabbit then discovers the PR is closed and edits its comment to include "Review failed — Pull request was closed or merged during review."

## Evidence

Observed on a managed private repo (12 most recent merged PRs) and the aidevops repo.

### Private repo — consistent ~76s merge pattern

| PR | CR comment created | PR merged | CR comment updated | CR outcome |
|----|-------------------|-----------|-------------------|------------|
| Representative sample | +13-14s | +76s | +111-194s | "Review failed — Pull request was closed or merged during review" |

Every PR shows the same pattern: CodeRabbit posts at ~14s, merge at ~76s (one poll interval + overhead), CodeRabbit edits comment post-merge. 7 of 7 sampled PRs had "Review failed" — zero completed CodeRabbit reviews.

### aidevops repo — fast merges with "Review skipped"

PRs #19239, #19240 merged in 21-23s. CodeRabbit posted "Review skipped — Auto reviews are limited based on label configuration." This also doesn't match `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` and is classified as a "real review."

### Classification logic (`do_check()` at line 361)

```
For each known bot that commented:
    bot_has_real_review() → checks if ANY comment is NOT a rate-limit notice
    If true → found_bots → unconditional PASS (line 388-391)
    If false → rate_limited_bots → configurable path (line 398-417)
```

CodeRabbit's placeholder hits the `found_bots` path — unconditional PASS, no configurability. The t2123 `review_gate` config has no effect here.

## Effects

1. **CHANGES_REQUESTED mechanism (t2093) is dead for these PRs:** CodeRabbit never submits a formal `reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED` because the PR is merged before Phase 2 completes. `_dispatch_pr_fix_worker()` never fires.

2. **Post-merge review scanner finds nothing:** CodeRabbit's final comment says "Review failed — No actionable comments were generated." The scanner correctly creates 0 followup issues — there are no findings to extract.

3. **Rate limit waste compounds:** CodeRabbit's Phase 1 processing (walkthrough generation, file analysis) likely counts against the hourly commit limit, burning quota on reviews that produce no findings. This triggers rate limits on subsequent PRs — the cascade described in GH#19173.

4. **Net result:** Zero CodeRabbit feedback on these PRs. Neither the pre-merge feedback loop (t2093) nor the post-merge scanner provides coverage.

## Root Cause

`bot_has_real_review()` (line 232) uses a negative filter: it checks if a comment matches known rate-limit patterns, and treats everything else as a real review. It has no concept of:
- Placeholder/stub comments that precede the actual review
- "Review failed" notices
- "Review skipped" notices
- The distinction between a comment existing and a review being complete

The `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` array (line 62-69) contains 6 patterns, all specific to quota/rate-limit language. Non-review bot messages that use different language pass through as false-positive "real reviews."

## Considerations

Several approaches could address this, each with different trade-offs. Leaving the design decision to maintainers:

- **Negative patterns approach:** Add "Review failed", "Review skipped", "closed or merged during review" to a non-review pattern list alongside the existing rate-limit patterns. Lightweight but continues the pattern-matching arms race — any new CodeRabbit message format would need a new pattern.

- **Positive signal approach:** Instead of "any comment that isn't rate-limited = real review," require a positive signal of a completed review (e.g., formal GitHub `reviewDecision` state, specific comment markers like CodeRabbit's walkthrough section, or `updated_at` > `created_at` indicating the comment has been edited with final content). More robust but more complex.

- **Minimum wait approach:** Introduce a configurable minimum time before the gate can pass (e.g., `REVIEW_BOT_MIN_WAIT=120`), giving bots time to complete Phase 2 regardless of what their Phase 1 comment contains. Simple to implement but adds latency to all merges, even when reviews complete quickly.

- **Comment age check:** Gate passes only if the bot's comment `updated_at` is older than a threshold (e.g., 30s), indicating the bot has finished editing. Targets the two-phase pattern specifically.

## Related

- GH#19173 — Discussion that identified the broader feedback gap (closed, partially addressed)
- PR #19186 / GH#19178 — Made rate-limit behavior configurable (t2123), but only affects the `rate_limited_bots` code path, not the `found_bots` false-positive path
- GH#17490 — Earlier review-bot-gate merge race (closed)
- t2093 — `CHANGES_REQUESTED` routing mechanism (working, but unreachable when reviews don't complete)

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.8.56
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0

title: fix: ISSUE_CONSOLIDATION_COMMENT_THRESHOLD defaults to 0 when pulse-triage.sh is sourced without pulse-wrapper.sh initialization
body:
## Problem

When `dispatch_with_dedup` is called from an LLM pulse session that sources `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` without the full `pulse-wrapper.sh` initialization, `ISSUE_CONSOLIDATION_COMMENT_THRESHOLD` is unset. The comparison `[[ $substantive_count -ge $ISSUE_CONSOLIDATION_COMMENT_THRESHOLD ]]` with an empty string treats the threshold as 0 — causing ANY substantive comment to trigger consolidation.

## Observed Impact

A single WORKER_SUPERSEDED comment (528 chars, passing the 200-char filter) triggered recursive consolidation:
- #961 → created #973, #974, #976 (3 cascade issues before stopped)
- #975 → created #977 (1 cascade issue before stopped)

## Fix

Add a default in `pulse-triage.sh`:

```bash
# In _issue_needs_consolidation():
local threshold="${ISSUE_CONSOLIDATION_COMMENT_THRESHOLD:-2}"
if [[ "$substantive_count" -ge "$threshold" ]]; then
```

Or add `ISSUE_CONSOLIDATION_COMMENT_THRESHOLD="${ISSUE_CONSOLIDATION_COMMENT_THRESHOLD:-2}"` to the module header.

## Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh` — add default value guard for `ISSUE_CONSOLIDATION_COMMENT_THRESHOLD` in `_issue_needs_consolidation()`

## Verification

- Source only `pulse-triage.sh` (without `pulse-wrapper.sh`) and call `_issue_needs_consolidation` on an issue with 1 substantive comment — should return 1 (no consolidation needed)
- The fix is a one-line change in `_issue_needs_consolidation`

## Context

This occurred during pulse cycle 2026-04-16T10:39-11:10Z. 4 cascade consolidation tasks had to be manually closed.

title: t2141: full-loop-helper merge — auto-resolve --admin/--auto mutual exclusion
body:
## Description

`full-loop-helper.sh merge` accepts both `--admin` and `--auto` pass-through flags (added in GH#18731 / PR #18757), but `gh pr merge` rejects them when both are set:

```
specify only one of `--auto`, `--disable-auto`, or `--admin`
```

This causes the wrapper to fail when a caller (or AI agent) plausibly passes both — e.g., "merge with admin override AND auto-merge if not yet ready". The flags express compatible intents in plain English; the agent has no signal that they're mutually exclusive at the CLI level.

## Reproduction

```bash
full-loop-helper.sh merge 19309 marcusquinn/aidevops --squash --admin --auto
# → "specify only one of `--auto`, `--disable-auto`, or `--admin`"
# → ERROR Merge failed for PR #19309
```

Observed live this session during the t2139 merge — re-running with just `--admin` succeeded.

## Proposed Fix

In `cmd_merge` (full-loop-helper.sh:1095), after parsing flags, detect the conflict and resolve it deterministically:

- When both `--admin` and `--auto` are set, prefer `--admin` and drop `--auto` (with an informational message).
- Rationale: `--admin` means "merge now via owner override"; `--auto` means "queue auto-merge to wait for checks". `--admin` already implies "now", so `--auto` is functionally redundant. Dropping it lets the merge proceed instead of erroring.

Document the resolution in the help text and the cmd_merge docstring.

## Files

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh:1095-1145` — `cmd_merge` flag parsing and help
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh:1157-1180` — `show_help` text
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-flag-conflict.sh` — regression test

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-flag-conflict.sh
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Conflict resolution: `--admin` + `--auto` → keeps `--admin`, drops `--auto` with informational message
- [ ] Help text documents the mutual exclusion
- [ ] Test asserts the resolution path
- [ ] shellcheck clean

title: t2140: register claude-opus-4-7 as opt-in model (defaults stay on 4.6)
body:
## Summary

Register Claude Opus 4.7 (released 2026-04-16) as a selectable option in the aidevops plugin without flipping any default tier mappings. All defaults continue to route to `claude-opus-4-6` where behaviour is known.

## Why not default?

Three concrete regressions vs 4.6 — the first two from Anthropic's own published data:

- **Long-context retrieval collapse** (MRCR v2 8-needle, Anthropic system card §8.7.2):
  - 256K: 91.9% → 59.2% (−32.7 pts)
  - 1M: 78.3% → 32.2% (−46.1 pts)
  - Makes 4.7 unsuitable for full-loop workers, cross-file refactors, and whole-repo audits.
- **Tokenizer bloat** (same paragraph under the new 4.7-only tokenizer):
  - English +58.8%, French +34%, Python code +21.4%, mixed multilingual +22.8%
  - CJK +4-6% (minor, old tokenizer was already inefficient there)
  - At identical per-token pricing this is a 20-60% effective cost increase on the framework's English-heavy prompts and issue bodies.
- **Stricter literal instruction-following** (Anthropic migration guide): prompts tuned for 4.6's looser interpretation may behave unexpectedly. The framework has 50+ headless dispatch scripts with prompts not yet audited for literal-mode safety.

## Scope of change

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-hook.mjs` — add `claude-opus-4-7` to `CLAUDE_MODEL_LIMITS` and both provider name maps
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/claude-proxy.mjs` — add `claude-opus-4-7` entry to `getClaudeProxyModels()`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/compare-models-helper.sh` — add to `MODEL_DATA` registry and `_api_model_string` case branch
- EDIT: `.agents/tools/ai-assistants/models-opus.md` — document "Opus 4.7 (opt-in)" section with the three tradeoffs

Context window is registered at **200K**, not the 1M API ceiling, so users opting in stay inside the still-functional retrieval window.

## What is NOT changed

- No tier mapping changes in `model-routing-table.json`, `aidevops.defaults.jsonc`, `fallback-chain-config.json.txt`, `shared-constants.sh`, `model-availability-helper.sh`, `contest-helper.sh`, or `fallback-chain-helper.sh`. All still route to `claude-opus-4-6`.
- No changes to the `opus` alias in `claude-proxy-context.mjs` MODEL_ALIASES.

Users who want to try 4.7 override via `custom/configs/model-routing-table.json`.

## Context

- Announcement: <https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-4-7>
- Migration guide: <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/migration-guide#migrating-to-claude-opus-4-7>
- Brief: `todo/tasks/t2140-brief.md`

## Agent doc simplification (automated scan)

**File:** `.agents/reference/pre-dispatch-validators.md`
**Detected topic:** Pre-Dispatch Validators
**Current size:** 108 lines

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

### For instruction docs — proposed action

Tighten and restructure this agent doc. Follow `tools/build-agent/build-agent.md` guidance. Key principles:

1. **Preserve all institutional knowledge** — every verbose rule exists because something broke without it. Do not remove task IDs, incident references, error statistics, or decision rationale. Compress prose, not knowledge.
2. **Order by importance** — most critical instructions first (primacy effect: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily). Security rules, core workflow, then edge cases.
3. **Split if needed** — if the file covers multiple distinct concerns, extract sub-docs with a parent index. Use progressive disclosure (pointers, not inline content).
4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers
3. **Zero content loss** — every line moves to a chapter file, nothing is deleted or compressed
4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

### Verification

- Content preservation: all code blocks, URLs, task ID references (`tNNN`, `GH#NNN`), and command examples must be present before and after
- No broken internal links or references
- Agent behaviour unchanged (test with a representative query if possible)

### Confidence: medium

Automated scan flagged this file for maintainer review. The best simplification strategy requires human judgment — some files are appropriately structured already. Reference corpora (SKILL.md, domain knowledge bases) need restructuring into chapters, not content reduction.

## Agent doc simplification (automated scan)

**File:** `.agents/reference/pre-dispatch-validators.md`
**Detected topic:** Pre-Dispatch Validators
**Current size:** 90 lines

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

### For instruction docs — proposed action

Tighten and restructure this agent doc. Follow `tools/build-agent/build-agent.md` guidance. Key principles:

1. **Preserve all institutional knowledge** — every verbose rule exists because something broke without it. Do not remove task IDs, incident references, error statistics, or decision rationale. Compress prose, not knowledge.
2. **Order by importance** — most critical instructions first (primacy effect: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily). Security rules, core workflow, then edge cases.
3. **Split if needed** — if the file covers multiple distinct concerns, extract sub-docs with a parent index. Use progressive disclosure (pointers, not inline content).
4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers
3. **Zero content loss** — every line moves to a chapter file, nothing is deleted or compressed
4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

### Verification

- Content preservation: all code blocks, URLs, task ID references (`tNNN`, `GH#NNN`), and command examples must be present before and after
- No broken internal links or references
- Agent behaviour unchanged (test with a representative query if possible)

title: t2145: add role:contributor guard to repos.json — gate scanners for non-maintainer instances
body:
## Problem

Contributor instances (e.g., milohiss) running aidevops with the aidevops repo in their repos.json cause their pulse's review-followup scanner to create 10+ NMR issues per day from Gemini medium-priority nits on already-merged PRs. This re-scrapes data the maintainer's own pulse already has. Historical close rate shows 34% NOT_PLANNED — high noise.

## Solution

Add `role` field to repos.json entries: `"maintainer"` (default for repos you own) or `"contributor"` (default for repos owned by others). Gate four scanner functions behind maintainer role:

- `_run_post_merge_review_scanner` (review-followup issues)
- `run_daily_codebase_review` (CodeRabbit review triggers)
- `run_weekly_complexity_scan` (simplification-debt issues)
- `run_simplification_dedup_cleanup` (dedup closures)

Contributors' pulses retain session-miner and memory-miner — data only the contributor has — which is the actual unique value channel.

## Implementation

PR #19350

title: consolidated: review-followup triage — BOLD top-level guard validity in 4 scripts (Phase 8c)
body:
_Supersedes #19275 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Triage the gemini-code-assist review bot suggestions from PR #19177 (t2053.8c BOLD readonly normalization batch 3) about adding `local BOLD` and `readonly BOLD` to the conditional BOLD guard in 4 scripts.

## Why

PR #19177 was merged with unaddressed gemini review bot comments on 4 files. The bot suggested replacing:
```bash
[[ -z "${BOLD+x}" ]] && BOLD='\033[1m'
```
with:
```bash
[[ -z "${BOLD+x}" ]] && { local BOLD; BOLD='\033[1m'; readonly BOLD; }
```
The bot's rationale: "separate local declaration from assignment for exit code safety" and "declare as readonly for immutability".

**Critical analysis:** The BOLD guard in all 4 files is at the **top level of the script** (not inside any function). `local` is only valid inside bash functions — using it at top level is a bash error. The bot's suggestion is factually incorrect for this code location.

## How

**Worker guidance — apply Outcome A (premise falsified):**

Verify each file at the listed line. Confirm the BOLD guard is at top-level (not inside a function). Then close this issue with the Outcome A comment template:

> **Premise falsified.** gemini-code-assist suggested `local BOLD` at file top-level. `local` is only valid inside bash functions — using it at script top-level is a bash error. The current `[[ -z "${BOLD+x}" ]] && BOLD='\033[1m'` guard is correct for top-level scope. Not acting.

**Files to verify:**

- `.agents/scripts/tool-version-check.sh:21` — `[[ -z "${BOLD+x}" ]] && BOLD='\033[1m'` at top-level (after source shared-constants.sh, before any function)
- `.agents/scripts/venv-health-check-helper.sh:32` — same pattern at top-level
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh:38` — same pattern at top-level
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-sessions.sh:28` — same pattern at top-level

**Pre-verification:** BOLD is not defined in shared-constants.sh (confirmed). The guard correctly handles the case where BOLD may be set in the calling environment.

**Note on readonly aspect:** The `readonly BOLD` portion of the suggestion is a separate concern from `local`. If desired, `readonly BOLD` (without `local`) could be added after the guard — this would be valid bash. However, this is a style preference, not a bug. The existing code functions correctly without it.

**No PR required for Outcome A.** Close the issue with the falsification comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Confirmed that BOLD guard lines are at top-level in all 4 files (not inside functions)
- [ ] Issue closed with Outcome A comment citing specific file:line evidence
- [ ] Parent #19275 already closed by consolidation task #19359

## Context & Decisions

- Source PR: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/19177 (t2053.8c, already merged)
- Review scanner (source:review-scanner) auto-created #19275 from unaddressed bot comments
- Consolidation task #19359 merged the thread into this spec (no substantive comments to preserve — bot-only thread)
- Bot suggestion uses `local` keyword which is invalid at script top-level in bash — this is a well-known gemini bot error on shell scripts that mix top-level and function-level code patterns
- The `[[ -z "${BOLD+x}" ]]` guard pattern is the correct framework idiom (see `prompts/build.txt` Quality Standards section) for top-level variable guards
